summary: Prolonged initial-response delay for chat completions after model artifact + runtime sync
description:
Issue summary: Customers report a noticeable increase in time-to-first-token (initial response) for chat completions immediately after a coordinated model artifact sync and runtime micro-release. Impact: Multiple BrightLegal tenants observed median initial-response latency go from ~80ms to 900-1200ms for short prompt chat sessions. Several sessions timed out at the client after default 3s, causing user-visible failures. This appears correlated with a rollout window where model artifacts were re-synced and runtime kernels were updated via a deploy.

Observed scope: - BrightLegal production (enterprise account) across multiple routes that pin to redwood-rt-3b-v2 and open-llama-7b-q4_0. - Elevated TTFB first noticed at 2026-03-11T02:47Z and reported at 2026-03-11T03:05Z.

Why this is high priority: Enterprise SLA impact (customer-facing product), reproduces reliably for affected model/runtime combinations, causes client timeouts and support escalations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a BrightLegal prod tenant, call the chat completions endpoint with a short completion prompt (~10 tokens expected) against model redwood-rt-3b-v2.
2) Use default client 3s timeout and standard batching (no special routing headers).
3) Observe initial token emission delay — client either receives first token after ~1s or times out at 3s depending on region and load.
4) Repeat against open-llama-7b-q4_0; behavior is similar but more variable across instances.
5) Pin runtime to previous build (rollback) and re-run — latency returns to baseline (~80-120ms TTFB).

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: coordinated artifact sync triggered kernel selection changes and forced a less-optimized execution path, causing synchronous priming of KV cache and extra blocking I/O on first requests.
SRE reproductions in staging showed increased latency only when runtime binary 1.9.2 was paired with newly published redwood-rt-3b-v2 artifacts; previous artifact/runtime pair did not reproduce.
Heap and GPU telemetry: no OOMs, but a noticeable increase in kernel-load time and blocking file I/O during first N requests post-sync (IOPS spike on model store).
Scheduler note: autoscaler briefly queued allocation which added ~500ms under low headroom; this amplified the per-request priming delay.
Temporary mitigation verified: pinning tenant routing to prior runtime binary 1.9.1 reduced median TTFB back to baseline for affected model routes.

Longer-term fix under investigation: - ensure model artifact warm-open on artifact publish (background mmap/prime). - improve kernel-selection handshake to avoid synchronous fallback when optimized kernels are hot-swapped. - add canary throttle to artifact sync so live traffic not exposed to simultaneous priming across nodes.

resolution: Workaround: Customer pinned tenant runtime to 1.9.1 which restored baseline TTFB. Fix: engineering merged PRs to (a) add artifact pre-warm background job on publish and (b) change kernel-selection to a non-blocking handshake with fallback telemetry. A staged canary rollout (5% traffic) executed 2026-03-12 and showed median TTFB back to baseline. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 after extended canary validation. Postmortem page created and follow-ups assigned for improving rollout throttles and adding an SLO alert for first-token latency.
